classification.description: 🥧 HTTPie CLI  — modern, user-friendly command-line HTTP client for the API era. JSON support, colors, sessions, downloads, plugins & more.

plan.architecture_summary: HTTPie CLI is a Python application designed for intuitive HTTP request construction and formatted terminal output. Entry points are registered in setup.cfg and invoke main execution through httpie.__main__ and httpie.core. Command-line flags, option parsing, and request construction are handled in httpie/cli. Output processing, syntax highlighting via Pygments/Rich, and stream writing are managed inside httpie/output. Persistent sessions, downloads, authentication, and file uploads are handled by dedicated modules like httpie/sessions.py and httpie/downloads.py. External shell completion and man page assets reside in the extras/ directory.

key_directories.purpose: Core Python package containing entry points, request processing, HTTP client wrappers, and session management.
Command-line option definitions, argument parsing logic, and CLI request item handling.
Formatting engines, syntax highlighting lexers, stream output writing, and terminal UI formatting.
Pytest unit and integration test suite testing CLI, client behavior, downloads, and output processing.
Shell auto-completions (bash, fish), man pages, and profiling scripts.

setup_steps.title: Clone the repository
setup_steps.detail: Clone your fork of the repository locally and enter the project folder.

setup_steps.title: Run initial setup and tests
setup_steps.detail: Creates a Python virtual environment in ./venv, installs dependencies in editable mode, and runs the test suite.

setup_steps.title: Activate virtual environment
setup_steps.detail: Activates the virtual environment for your shell session so that the 'http' binary points to your local working copy.

setup_steps.title: Run unit tests
setup_steps.detail: Runs pytest across the HTTPie codebase with test coverage options.

setup_steps.title: Check code style
setup_steps.detail: Runs flake8 to verify PEP8 compliance across source code and test files.

branch: Fork the repository and create a new feature branch for your changes (e.g., git checkout -b my_topical_branch).
Target the master branch when opening pull requests.
commit: Add your name to AUTHORS.md if you wish to be listed as a contributor.
pull_request: Code changes must include corresponding unit/integration tests in tests/.
Interface or behavior modifications must update documentation.
Consider adding a CHANGELOG.md entry describing your change.
Ensure all GitHub Actions automated CI checks pass.
code_style: Run flake8 checks using make codestyle.
Run test suite with pytest using make test or python -m pytest.

issues.title: fish shell completions
issues.why: Ideal beginner task touching shell script completions with precedent in recent merged PRs.
issues.approach: Inspect extras/httpie-completion.fish alongside extras/httpie-completion.bash. Add fish shell completions for missing options or command aliases, then verify completion behavior using fish.

issues.title: Compact help
issues.why: Direct fit for Python beginners learning HTTPie's CLI argument parsing and option definition structure.
issues.approach: Examine httpie/cli/argparser.py and httpie/cli/definition.py to locate usage generation logic. Introduce or refine compact usage/help output formatting and add unit tests under tests/ to verify output.

issues.title: --pretty=all piped to a pager does not work on Windows
issues.why: Good opportunity to explore Python output formatting, stream handling, and platform-specific terminal quirks.
issues.approach: Inspect terminal color and paging detection in httpie/output/writer.py and httpie/output/streams.py when stdout is redirected or piped on Windows. Update stream coloring logic to handle Windows pipe streams properly and add corresponding unit tests.

first_timer_insights: Recent merged first-time PRs frequently involve documentation fixes (e.g., docs/README.md), shell completion enhancements (extras/httpie-completion.fish), or small targeted Python fixes.
Maintainers favor small, self-contained PRs with high test coverage and minimal code churn.
caveats: Windows users must run venv creation and pip installation commands manually instead of using the Unix Makefile.
Some issues marked 'help wanted' (e.g. compact help design) may require maintainer input on exact UI/formatting preference before final implementation.
